docs.title: UCI Nature Wildlife Pipeline
docs.text: A backend Python pipeline for processing wildlife camera images.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This project processes wildlife camera images, reduces manual review, and generates structured CSV outputs. The backend pipeline indexes files, downloads images when needed, builds manifests, runs wildlife classification, and writes results into the output folders.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: The goal is to turn large image collections into structured CSV results that are easier to review and share. The main outputs are written under data/outputs/, including per-camera CSV files in data/outputs/by_location/.

docs.title: Run paths
docs.text:
You can run the pipeline in two main ways:

  1. from images copied locally from an SD card or another folder on your computer
  2. from images retrieved from Google Drive

For this docs site, ignore the frontend, UI, Docker, and deployment parts of the repository.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Install Python 3.11 and the project dependencies.
  2. Run the local-folder workflow or the Google Drive workflow.
  3. Check the CSV outputs in data/outputs/ and data/outputs/by_location/.

docs.title: UCI-NATURE — Run, Deploy & Smoke Test Cheat Sheet
docs.text: This is the quick reference for running the plain HTML/CSS/JS UI locally and deploying the same code to AWS behind Caddy + Docker. The frontend is not React/Vite — it's static files served by nginx in production and any static server during local dev.

docs.title: 1. Local development
docs.text:
You need two processes: the FastAPI backend on 127.0.0.1:8000 and any static file server (or Python's built-in one) for ui/index.html.

# Terminal 1 — backend
cd ~/UCI-NATURE
source .venv311/bin/activate          # or your preferred venv
pip install -r requirements/requirements.txt
uvicorn ui.backend.main:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

# Terminal 2 — static UI on http://127.0.0.1:5500
cd ~/UCI-NATURE/ui
python3 -m http.server 5500
# Then open http://127.0.0.1:5500/  in your browser

The frontend auto-detects local dev (hostname 127.0.0.1 / localhost) and talks to the backend at http://127.0.0.1:8000. On any other hostname it falls back to same-origin /api, which is what Caddy serves on AWS.

docs.title: Override the API base (optional)
docs.text:
Add this to the top of <head> in ui/index.html if you ever need to point the UI at a different backend (e.g., a staging tunnel):

<meta name="uci-nature-backend-base" content="https://my-tunnel.example.com">

docs.title: 2. AWS Docker deploy
docs.text:
The production target is https://uci-nature-pipeline.duckdns.org. The whole stack is three containers managed by docker compose in docker/:

  • backend — FastAPI on port 8000 (internal only)
  • frontend — nginx serving ui/ on port 80 (internal only)
  • caddy — public ingress on ports 80/443, proxies /api to backend and everything else to nginx, terminates TLS

docs.title: Build & deploy from ~/UCI-NATURE/docker
docs.text:
cd ~/UCI-NATURE/docker

# Pull latest code first
git -C ~/UCI-NATURE pull --ff-only

# Rebuild and restart everything (forces fresh frontend image with latest UI)
docker compose build --no-cache frontend
docker compose up -d --force-recreate

# Or, if only the backend changed:
docker compose build backend
docker compose up -d --force-recreate backend

docs.title: Useful inspection commands
docs.text:
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f caddy
docker compose logs -f backend
docker compose logs -f frontend

# Confirm the new UI is actually inside the container
docker compose exec frontend sh -c 'grep UCI_NATURE_ASSET_VERSION /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html || head -20 /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html'

docs.title: Forcing browsers to flush stale assets
docs.text: Each deploy should bump the ?v=... query string on the asset references in ui/index.html (look for 20260515-1). The nginx and Caddy configs now also emit Cache-Control: no-store for HTML responses, so users will always pull a fresh index.html and pick up the new versioned URLs on next reload.

docs.title: 3. Backend API smoke test
docs.text:
Run from your dev machine (or from inside the caddy network on AWS). Replace BASE to switch targets.

BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8000        # local dev
# BASE=https://uci-nature-pipeline.duckdns.org   # AWS

# 1. Health
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/health" | jq .

# 2. Local (guest) login — returns access_token
TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$BASE/api/auth/login" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"","project":"uci"}' | jq -r .access_token)
echo "TOKEN=$TOKEN"

# 3. Who am I (should echo {"project":"uci"})
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/auth/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

# 4. Drive status (guest mode → connected:false, google_authenticated:false)
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/drive/status" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

# 5. Google OAuth start URL (only useful if google creds are configured)
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/auth/google/start" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

# 6. Pipeline status
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/pipeline/status" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

# 7. Dashboard summary
curl -fsS "$BASE/api/dashboard/summary" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .

If /api/health fails on AWS, Caddy isn't routing /api correctly — check docker/Caddyfile and docker compose logs caddy.

docs.title: 4. Browser smoke test checklist
docs.text:
Run through this after every deploy with DevTools → Network open and Disable cache checked.

  1. Visit https://uci-nature-pipeline.duckdns.org/.
  2. Network: index.html shows Cache-Control: no-store.
  3. Network: main.js?v=... and all *.css?v=... requests return 200.
  4. Console: prints App start then Markup loaded. No red errors.
  5. The boot splash disappears and the login card appears.
  6. Click Continue → step 2 shows the "Connect Google Drive" and "Continue as Guest" buttons.
  7. Click Continue as Guest.
  8. Network: POST /api/auth/login returns 200 with an access_token.
  9. You land on the Dashboard / Upload page.
  10. Click Connect Google Drive (in another session).
  11. Network: POST /api/auth/login then GET /api/auth/google/start return 200; browser redirects to accounts.google.com.
  12. After OAuth callback you should land on the Drive confirm modal. Click Confirm & Enter Dashboard.
  13. Network: POST /api/drive/connect returns 200 with connected: true.
  14. Pick a Drive folder → click Sync.
  15. Network: POST /api/drive/sync returns 200.
  16. The Drive sync card switches to "Syncing…" and the percentage advances.
  17. Navigate to Run Model, Review, Validate, Export, Statistics — each page renders without console errors.

docs.title: Common console signs to watch for
docs.text:
• startGoogleSignIn is not defined — you're on a stale index.html. Hard-reload (Cmd-Shift-R / Ctrl-F5). If it persists, check that the deployed index.html includes the inline pre-bind shim (search the page source for __uciNatureFlushDeferred).
  • Failed to load partial: … — a feature partial 404'd. Confirm the nginx container actually has ui/src/features/... files (docker compose exec frontend ls /usr/share/nginx/html/src/features).
  • Mixed content warnings — backend base resolved to http://... while the page loaded over HTTPS. Verify Caddy is terminating TLS and that the UI is using the same-origin /api path (default on non-localhost hostnames).

docs.title: Run
docs.text: The backend Python pipeline is the main workflow.

docs.title: A. Local SD card or local folder workflow
docs.text: Use this when images were copied from an SD card or already exist in a local folder on the computer.

docs.title: Step 1: activate the environment
docs.text:
cd /path/to/UCI-NATURE
source .venv311/bin/activate

docs.title: Step 2: create the local input folder
docs.text:
mkdir -p data/local_input
mkdir -p data/staging
mkdir -p data/outputs/by_location

Copy SD card images into:

data/local_input/

docs.title: Step 3: clean old outputs
docs.text:
rm -rf data/staging/*
rm -f data/outputs/manifest.csv
rm -f data/outputs/manifest_new.csv
rm -f data/outputs/metadata.csv
rm -f data/outputs/ml_outputs.csv
rm -f data/outputs/speciesnet_results.json
rm -f data/outputs/speciesnet_results.csv
rm -f data/outputs/speciesnet_review.csv
rm -f data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json
rm -f data/outputs/logs/unmatched_predictions.csv
rm -rf data/outputs/by_location
mkdir -p data/outputs/by_location

docs.title: Step 4: run the pipeline in manual mode
docs.text:
python3 scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py --mode manual --folder "/path/to/UCI-NATURE/data/local_input"

The main outputs go to:

data/outputs/
data/outputs/by_location/

docs.title: B. Google Drive workflow
docs.text: Use this when the source images are still in Google Drive.

docs.title: Full run command
docs.text:
echo "Running full Drive pipeline..."
python3 scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py

docs.title: Step by step command
docs.text:
cd /path/to/UCI-NATURE
source .venv311/bin/activate
python3 scripts/pipeline/build_index.py
python3 scripts/pipeline/download_drive.py --index data/outputs/drive_index.csv
python3 scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py

docs.title: What the pipeline does internally
docs.text:
When the full Drive pipeline runs, it performs these steps:

  1. build Drive index
  2. download images into local staging
  3. create the manifest
  4. extract EXIF metadata
  5. run SpeciesNet
  6. postprocess SpeciesNet results
  7. generate inference CSVs
  8. merge metadata again
  9. write final per-location CSV outputs

You can also run the Drive-based flow through the main entry point only:

cd /path/to/UCI-NATURE
source .venv311/bin/activate
python3 scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py

docs.title: C. Testing and verification commands
docs.text: Use these commands to verify that the environment, inputs, and outputs are correct.

docs.title: Check that the environment is active
docs.text:
which python
python --version

docs.title: Check required imports
docs.text:
python -c "from PIL import Image; print('Pillow ok')"
python -c "from google.oauth2 import service_account; print('google-auth ok')"

docs.title: Check that local input has images
docs.text:
find data/local_input -type f | head
find data/local_input -type f | wc -l

docs.title: Check that staging has images
docs.text:
find data/staging -type f | head
find data/staging -type f | wc -l

docs.title: Check output files were created
docs.text:
ls data/outputs
ls data/outputs/by_location

docs.title: Preview the first few rows of a result CSV
docs.text: head -n 5 data/outputs/by_location/*.csv

docs.title: Check manifest row count
docs.text: wc -l data/outputs/manifest.csv

docs.title: Check ML summary
docs.text: cat data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json

docs.title: Open the output folder
docs.text: open data/outputs/by_location

docs.title: D. Batch run option
docs.text:
Runs the full pipeline automatically for a batch manifest.

./run_batch.sh batch_0001.csv

Batch CSV files come from:

data/outputs/batches/

docs.title: E. Test CSV generation
docs.text:
Creates fake output CSVs without running ML.

python create_test_csvs.py

Use this when you want sample output files for testing.

docs.title: F. Output files
docs.text:
Check these files after a run:

Path What you should find data/outputs/manifest.csv File inventory for the current run data/outputs/metadata.csv EXIF metadata plus merged ML fields data/outputs/ml_outputs.csv Flattened inference results data/outputs/speciesnet_review.csv Review-oriented output from SpeciesNet post-processing data/outputs/by_location/ Final per-camera or per-location CSV exports data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json Summary counts for processed images and ML results

docs.title: G. Notes
docs.text:
• Use --mode manual --folder ... for SD card or local folder runs.
  • Use python scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py for the normal Google Drive flow.
  • Do not point manual mode at data/staging/, because the pipeline copies files into staging and will try to copy files onto themselves.
  • python scripts/pipeline/download_images.py is outdated in this project. Use python scripts/pipeline/download_drive.py --index data/outputs/drive_index.csv instead.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Use Python 3.11 for this project.

docs.title: Clone the repo
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ralkhleef/UCI-NATURE.git
cd UCI-NATURE

docs.title: Create a virtual environment
docs.text: python3 -m venv .venv

docs.title: Activate the environment
docs.text:
macOS / LinuxWindows PowerShell 
source .venv/bin/activate

.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

docs.title: Install dependencies
docs.text:
python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.ml.cpu.lock.txt

docs.title: Check Python
docs.text: python3 --version

docs.title: Drive mode only
docs.text:
If you want to pull images from Google Drive, keep the service account file in:

secrets/inf191a-uci-nature-sa.json

You can also set the path with UCI_NATURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE.

docs.title: pip not found
docs.text: python3 -m pip install -r requirements

docs.title: Venv not activating
docs.text:
Create a fresh virtual environment and activate it.

python3.11 -m venv .venv311
source .venv311/bin/activate

docs.title: Wrong Python version
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11.

python3 --version
python3.11 --version

docs.title: Missing dependencies
docs.text:
Install the project requirements from the repository root.

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements/requirements.txt

If the project depends on the locked environment, use:

python -m pip install -r requirements/requirements.lock

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'
docs.text:
PIL comes from Pillow.

python -m pip install pillow

Or reinstall the project requirements:

python -m pip install -r requirements/requirements.txt

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'google'
docs.text:
This usually means the Google auth packages are missing.

python -m pip install google-auth google-api-python-client

Or reinstall the project requirements:

python -m pip install -r requirements

docs.title: Script path issues
docs.text:
Run commands from the repository root:

cd "/Users/yourname/Desktop/UCI-NATURE"

docs.title: Folder does not exist: /absolute/path/to/images
docs.text:
This means the example placeholder path was used literally. Replace it with a real local folder path.

Example:

python scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py --mode manual --folder "/Users/yourname/path/to/images"

You can drag the folder from Finder into Terminal to paste the full path.

docs.title: SameFileError when using manual mode
docs.text:
Do not point manual mode at data/staging. Manual mode copies files into data/staging, so using staging as the source causes the script to copy a file onto itself.

Wrong:

python scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py --mode manual --folder "/Users/.../data/staging"

Use a separate input folder instead:

python scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py --mode manual --folder "/Users/.../data/local_input"

docs.title: Pipeline runs but processes 0 images
docs.text:
Check whether the input folder is empty.

For local/manual mode:

find data/local_input -type f | head
find data/local_input -type f | wc -l

For Drive mode:

find data/staging -type f | head
find data/staging -type f | wc -l

If no images are listed, the pipeline has nothing to process.

docs.title: download_images.py not found
docs.text:
Use the actual Drive download script instead:

python scripts/pipeline/download_drive.py --index data/outputs/drive_index.csv

Or just run the full pipeline entry point:

python scripts/pipeline/run_pipeline.py

docs.title: Drive permissions or service account issues
docs.text:
• Check secrets/inf191a-uci-nature-sa.json
  • Check UCI_NATURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE if you changed the path
  • Make sure the Drive folder is shared with the service account
  • Re-run python scripts/pipeline/build_index.py after confirming access

docs.title: zsh: no matches found
docs.text:
This happens when trying to remove files with a wildcard in an empty folder.

Example:

rm -rf data/staging/*

If the folder is already empty, zsh may show:

zsh: no matches found

This is usually harmless. You can continue.

docs.title: Pipeline runs but no CSV output appears
docs.text:
Check the main output files:

ls data/outputs
ls data/outputs/by_location

Also check:

  • data/outputs/manifest.csv
  • data/outputs/metadata.csv
  • data/outputs/ml_outputs.csv
  • data/outputs/by_location/

You can also re-run the output generation step:

python scripts/pipeline/make_output.py --manifest data/outputs/manifest.csv --metadata data/outputs/metadata.csv --drive_index data/outputs/drive_index.csv --out_dir data/outputs/by_location --burst_seconds 300 --burst_export all

docs.title: Pipeline finishes but data/staging is empty
docs.text:
That can be normal. The pipeline may clear data/staging after a successful run while keeping outputs in:

data/outputs/
data/outputs/by_location/

docs.title: SpeciesNet is taking a long time
docs.text: That is normal for larger image sets or slower hardware. Watch the progress bars and wait for the run to finish before assuming it is stuck.

docs.title: Pipeline fails mid-run
docs.text:
• Check the last script that failed
  • Re-run that step from the repository root
  • Inspect files in data/outputs/
  • Check data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json and data/outputs/logs/unmatched_predictions.csv

Useful checks:

ls data/outputs
cat data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json

docs.title: Check outputs after a successful run
docs.text:
ls data/outputs
ls data/outputs/by_location
cat data/outputs/logs/ml_summary.json

To preview the first few rows of the final CSVs:

head -n 5 data/outputs/by_location/*.csv

docs.title: Batch run issues
docs.text:
• Make sure the batch CSV exists in data/outputs/batches/
  • Check the filename passed to ./run_batch.sh
  • Make sure the virtual environment is available before running the script

Example:

./run_batch.sh batch_0001.csv
